_meta.indication: SIVEXTRO is an oxazolidinone-class antibacterial drug indicated in adults for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by designated susceptible Gram-positive bacteria including S. aureus (MRSA and MSSA), S. pyogenes, S. agalactiae, S. anginosus group, and E. faecalis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter, noninferiority trial; oral tedizolid phosphate 200 mg daily x 6 days vs oral linezolid 600 mg bid x 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response at the 48-72 Hour Visit in the ITT population (cessation of lesion spread plus afebrile status), noninferiority margin -10%
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response 256/323 (79.3%) tedizolid vs 258/326 (79.1%) linezolid; treatment difference 0.1% [adjusted 95% CI: -6.2%, 6.3%] — met prespecified NI margin

nct_ctgov.title: TR-701 FA vs. Linezolid for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, multicenter, noninferiority trial; IV-to-oral tedizolid phosphate 200 mg daily x 6 days vs IV-to-oral linezolid 600 mg bid x 10 days
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Early clinical response at the 48-72 Hour Visit in the ITT population, defined as >=20% reduction in lesion area; noninferiority margin -10%
pivotal_trials.result: Early clinical response (>=20% lesion reduction) 283/332 (85.2%) tedizolid vs 276/334 (82.6%) linezolid; treatment difference 2.6% [unadjusted 95% CI: -3.0%, 8.2%] — met prespecified NI margin

nct_ctgov.title: TR-701 FA vs Linezolid for the Treatment of Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=2%) were nausea (8%), headache (6%), diarrhea (4%), vomiting (3%), and dizziness (2%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 12/662 (1.8%) treated with SIVEXTRO vs 13/662 (2.0%) comparator; SIVEXTRO discontinued due to an adverse reaction in 3/662 (0.5%).
target_moa: Tedizolid is an oxazolidinone-class antibacterial; its activity is mediated by binding to the 50S subunit of the bacterial ribosome, resulting in inhibition of bacterial protein synthesis.
modality: small molecule (oxazolidinone-class antibacterial; prodrug tedizolid phosphate)

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management determined that a REMS for the management of risks associated with tedizolid was not recommended, based on a safety profile consistent with linezolid, which does not have a REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee met March 31, 2014; all committee members voted 'Yes' that the applicant provided substantial evidence of the safety and effectiveness of tedizolid phosphate for the treatment of ABSSSI.

summary.text: Tedizolid phosphate (NDA 205435) was granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation under the GAIN Act for ABSSSI and HABP/VABP, which conferred priority review and an additional five years of marketing exclusivity. The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee met March 31, 2014 and voted unanimously 'Yes' on substantial evidence of safety and effectiveness; the application was approved first cycle based on two Phase 3 noninferiority trials versus linezolid, with pediatric and antimicrobial resistance surveillance postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: tedizolid tablets and powder for injection were granted Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation and therefore this application was granted a priority review. QIDP designation qualifies tedizolid for an additional five years of marketing exclusivity.
The Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, met on March 31, 2014.

All committee members voted “Yes”, indicating that the applicant provided substantial evidence of the safety and effectiveness of tedizolid phosphate for the treatment of acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections caused by susceptible isolates of the designated microorganisms.
Therefore, non-inferiority of tedizolid phosphate to linezolid is demonstrated in both Study TR 701-112 and Study TR 701-113.
